Apple CEO Tim Cook announced today that Apple will donate funds to support disaster relief efforts in Indonesia following the major earthquake. Details below.

Apple to donate to Indonesia earthquake relief efforts

Over the past few years, Apple has consistently donated to assist relief efforts following major earthquakes, floods, and other emergencies around the world.

In just the past two months alone, the company has supported relief efforts in Venezuela, Southern Europe, and Japan. Apple CEO Tim Cook announced today that the company will also be donating to relief efforts in Indonesia in response to the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck over the weekend.

As is customary, Cook did not specify the amount of Apple's donation or the organizations that will benefit.

9to5Mac Take

Beyond donating after natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal giving program called "Employee Giving," which has raised over US$880 million to date through the company's donation matching policy.

Since Tim Cook announced his decision to step down as Apple CEO, there has been much discussion about the legacy he leaves behind. Apple's commitment to philanthropic and humanitarian work has been an important part of his tenure, and it is hoped this will continue under John Ternus's leadership.
